To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
, for the linearized optical field in a nonlinear OFC system, the noise impact is accurately evaluated by calculating the moment-generating function directly from the noise equation.
the MGF can be calculated accurately from LNE with EDFAs.
, for the linearized noise amplified in EDFAs, we propose an efficient method to obtain its MGF, and our results agree with the experimental data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the accurate evaluation of noise impact in OFC systems with signal much stronger than noise.
the MGF of linearized noise and its impact on the system.
the MGF calculation of the linearized noise amplified in EDFAs, which is important for evaluating the impact of the optical noise on the performance of OFC systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MGF method can be applied to evaluate the linearized noise amplified in EDFAs with high accuracy, if the accurate LNE is employed.
the MGF method can accurately evaluate the impact on the system of the linearized noise amplified in the optical fibers, and it is not necessary to use the CW approximation in the calculation.
the MGF method based on the accurate LNE can be used to accurately evaluate linearized noise impact in the OFC systems with signal power much higher than noise power.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for the cases of both linearized noise amplified in optical fibers and linearized noise amplified after optical preamplifiers, MGF method based on the accurate LNE can provide more accurate system performances than those obtained from the LNE with CW approximation.
the accurate LNE is the key to accurately calculate the impact of optical noise on the system performance, which is also the basis for the development of accurate nonlinear noise models.
, the accurate LNE can be used to obtain the MGF for the noise amplified by EDAFs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, the MGF method is a powerful tool for evaluating the noise impact of a nonlinear fiber communication system, provided that the noise propagator is calculated accurately.
the MGF method is very useful for accurately predicting the performance of nonlinear optical fiber communication systems with signal much stronger than the noise.
the MGF method based on the LNOE with CW approximation is not reliable for evaluating the impact of linearized noise in a multi-span OFC system.
